summary: Seiji Kumagai works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned a PhD from Kyoto University, where he studied around 2005–2008 and later served as an associate professor (准教授) from around 2013 to 2022.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology, Seiji Nemoto studied at Meiji University from around 1968 to 1972. He later served as a professor at the University of Tsukuba from around 2000 to 2015.
Seijun Ishii is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Komazawa University from around 1977 to 1981. He later became a professor at Komazawa University around 2003.

Seiko Hirata worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying at Kyoto University from around 1947 to 1950 under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu. He later held a post at Hanazono University from around 1970 to 1995.

Seiren Matsunami specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and under Walther Schubring. He served as a professor at Kyushu University (~1949–1967) and Rissho University (~1967–1974), and lectured at Taisho University.

Seishi Karashima specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology, studying at the University of Tokyo, Cambridge, and Peking University under mentors including Xianlin Ji and Oskar von Hinüber. He held posts at the Eastern Institute and Soka University (~1996–2019).
Seishin Kato was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University from around 1896 to 1899. He later held academic posts at Toyo University (~1904–1926) and Taisho University (~1926–1943).
Seitatsu Matsunami is an Indologist and Tibetologist. He served as an assistant (助手) at the University of Tokyo and as a professor (教授) at Taisho University (attested in 1992).

Seitetsu Moriyama specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts at Bukkyo University, serving as a professor in 2002 and attested there in 2004 and in the Department of Buddhist Studies in 2013.

Seizan Yanagida worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology, studying at Hanazono University (~1942–1945). He served as a professor, director, and professor emeritus at Hanazono University, as a professor at Kyoto University (attested 1986–1988), and at Chubu University (~1988–1993).
Sen Wang worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Peking University from around 1932 to 1936, he served as a professor at Minzu University of China from around 1952 to 1986.

Senarat Wijayasundara is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 1999, he was attested as a teacher at the University of Kelaniya and as a visiting lecturer at the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.

Senchu Murano was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1929–1933) and the University of Washington (~1934–1938). He later served as a professor at Rissho University from around 1957 to 1979.

Sengaku Maeda worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo, UPenn (PhD), and Münster. He held faculty posts at UPenn, Tokyo, and Musashino University, and chaired Bukkyō Dendō Kyōkai (1995–2016).

Senkei Sakawa specialized in Buddhist studies, completing studies at Rissho University by 1965. He later served as a professor in the Department of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University, attested from 1981 to 1985.

Senmyo Naniwa specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University, studying under Purushottam Vishvanath Bapat, Genjun Sasaki, and others. In 2005, he was attested as a researcher at the Eastern Institute and professor at Bukkyo University.
Sensho Hibi specialized in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Rissho University from around 1955 to 1959 and later served as an assistant professor (助教授) there from around 1968 to 1976.
Sensho Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Otani University from around 1962 to 1970. He later served as a professor at Otani University from around 1986 to 2014.

Sensho Murakami worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Toyo University (~1887–1890) and held posts at Sendan-Rin School, Toyo University, Tokyo Imperial University, Otani University, and the University of Tokyo (including professor, 1917–1922).

Seok-hyeong Kim worked in religious and Buddhist studies, studying at Taisho University from around 1927 to 1931. He served as a part-time lecturer at Seoul National University and as a professor at Dongguk University.
